profile.capacity_note: not published by the operator at the building level. Per CloudHQs own current page for the LC Campus (tier-1 operator source, https://cloudhq.com/campus/lc-campus/), this campus is in the heart of Ashburn, Virginia, directly off Loudoun County Parkway, and totals about 8.5 million square feet and 1,256 MW of total critical IT load across fourteen data centers, with 756 MW available critical load, as of this sessions retrieval. profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 38 (CloudHQ VA missing-address campaign): identified this as one of a cluster of planned buildings sharing a Baxtel sourced project address with LC9, refreshed company history from the operators own about and founder pages, flagged a second CloudHQ name collision on Wikipedia not present in a prior sessions notes. research_status remains complete.

[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CloudHQ, the data center operator, was established in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, per the operators own current about page (cloudhq.com/about/) fetched fresh this session. Fateh previously served as CEO and co-founder of DuPont Fabros Technology, a data center company that sold for 7.8 billion dollars in 2017, and has built and operated more than 700 MW of data center capacity across his career, per CloudHQs own founder page (cloudhq.com/learn-about-our-founder/), also fetched fresh this session. CloudHQ operates as part of the Fateh Family Office, alongside affiliated companies CloudCapital, WindHQ, and Dalian Development, per the operators own about page. The company maintains three regional headquarters, a global headquarters in Washington DC, an EMEA headquarters in London, and an APAC headquarters in Singapore. Per the operators own current about page, CloudHQ now describes 23 global campuses, more than 1,380 MW of contracted critical IT load with more than 6,000 MW of expansion potential, more than 30 million square feet of global data center portfolio, and more than 330 employees. A prior research pass on these rows had already flagged that the domain cloudhq.net resolves to an unrelated Google Workspace and Gmail backup software company, not this data center operator, and correctly redirected to cloudhq.com. This session found a second, separate name collision worth flagging for a future researcher: the Wikipedia article at en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CloudHQ describes yet another different, unrelated company, a cloud data synchronization tool for Google Workspace founded in 2011 by Senad Dizdar and based in San Francisco, not this Ashburn and Manassas Virginia data center operator founded by Hossein Fateh. That Wikipedia article was checked this session and found not to apply, so it is not used or cited as a source here, and no Wikipedia sourced company history is included in this reading. This specific row, LC10, per Baxtels own dedicated LC10 data center page (baxtel.com/data-center/cloudhq-lc10), fetched fresh this session, is a planned building that Baxtel states will be part of CloudHQs Ashburn Data Center Campus located at 22210 Loudoun County Parkway, Ashburn, Virginia. Baxtels own dedicated LC9 page gives this identical address for LC9, a neighboring planned building in the same registry, so this address identifies the shared project site rather than a number distinguishing LC10 specifically from LC9, flagged here rather than silently treated as building specific. DataCenterMap separately lists a CloudHQ LC10 facility in Ashburn without its own distinct street address.

reading.body:
CloudHQ LC10 is a planned data center building in Ashburn, Virginia, part of the fourteen-building LC Campus that together publish 1,256 MW of total critical IT load with 756 MW available for new tenants. The operator has not published capacity specifications for LC10 individually. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the campus's 756 MW of available capacity would support roughly 18,900 racks, though this figure applies to the entire LC Campus rather than LC10 alone and represents an assumption about workload type rather than an operator specification.

LC10's status as a planned rather than operational facility means it does not yet contribute to Virginia's grid load or to the 1,375 MW of published data center capacity mapped across the state. CloudHQ operates the LC Campus in the core of Northern Virginia's Ashburn cluster, where grid constraints and power availability now determine expansion pace across the region's 326 mapped facilities.

The building's significance depends on execution timelines and power allocation that are not published. No certifications, grid interconnection details, power source, or operational date have been disclosed in the operator's published specifications.
